nodes.summary: Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ be nonzero integers such that $\beta \ne \gamma \alpha^k$ and $\beta \alpha^k \ne \gamma$ for every natural number $k$, that is, $\beta / \gamma$ is not $\alpha^k$ for any integer $k$. Then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p$ divides none of the integers $\gamma \alpha^n - \beta$ with $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many primes avoid $\gamma \alpha^n - \beta$

nodes.summary: Let $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, and write $u^{(n)}$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then $u$ is nilpotent at $r$ if $u^{(n)}(r) = 0$ for some $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent polynomial at a point

nodes.summary: Let $u(x) = x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and write $u^{(m)}$ for the $m$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then for every prime $p$ there is $m \ge 1$ such that $p$ divides $u^{(m)}(1)$.
nodes.title: $x + 1$ is locally nilpotent at $1$

nodes.summary: Let $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. Write $u^{(m)}$ for the $m$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then $u$ is weakly locally nilpotent at $r$ outside $A$ if for every prime $p \notin A$ there is $m \ge 1$ such that $p$ divides $u^{(m)}(r)$. For $A = \emptyset$ this is called locally nilpotent at $r$.
nodes.title: Weakly locally nilpotent polynomial at a point

nodes.summary: Let $u(x) = x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and write $u^{(m)}$ for its $m$-fold iterate as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. For every integer $r$ and every natural number $m$, $u^{(m)}(r) = r + m$.
nodes.title: Iterates of $x + 1$

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of primes, and let $c$ range over the positive integers all of whose prime factors lie in $A$. A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $1$ is weakly locally nilpotent at $1$ outside $A$ and not nilpotent at $1$ if and only if $u$ is one of: $x + c$; $x - c$ with $c \ne 1$; $cx + 1$ or $-cx + 1$ with $c \ne 1$; or $-2x - 1$, the last only when $2 \in A$.
nodes.title: Linear polynomials weakly locally nilpotent but not nilpotent at $1$

nodes.summary: A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of positive degree is locally nilpotent at $-1$ if and only if it has one of the following forms, for some $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$: $(x+1)p(x)$ with $p \ne 0$; $-2x - 4 + p(x)(x+1)(x+2)$; $2x^2 + 7x + 3 + p(x)(x+1)(x+2)(x+3)$; or $u = x - 1$.
nodes.title: Classification of locally nilpotent polynomials at $-1$

nodes.summary: A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of positive degree is locally nilpotent at $1$ if and only if it has one of the following forms, for some $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$: $(x-1)p(x)$ with $p \ne 0$; $-2x + 4 + p(x)(x-1)(x-2)$; $-2x^2 + 7x - 3 + p(x)(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$; or $u = x + 1$.
nodes.title: Classification of locally nilpotent polynomials at $1$

nodes.summary:

e 0$, and…
nodes.title: Classification of locally nilpotent polynomials at $0$

nodes.summary: The only polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of positive degree that is locally nilpotent at $1$ but not nilpotent at $1$ is $x + 1$, and the only polynomial of positive degree that is locally nilpotent at $-1$ but not nilpotent at $-1$ is $x - 1$.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent but not nilpotent polynomials at $\pm 1$

nodes.summary: A polynomial $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree at least $1$ is locally nilpotent at $0$ and not nilpotent at $0$ if and only if either $u = x + b$ for some integer $b \ne 0$, or $u = ax + b$ for some integers $a$ and $b$ with $b \ne 0$ such that $a$ has at least one prime divisor and every prime divisor of $a$ divides $b$.
nodes.title: Polynomials locally nilpotent but not nilpotent at $0$

nodes.summary: The polynomial $x + 1 \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is not nilpotent at $1$.
nodes.title: $x + 1$ is not nilpotent at $1$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
